newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ACCC sees Bank Melbourne decision soon.
newsitem.headline: ACCC sees Bank Melbourne decision soon.

text.p: Australia's anti-monopolies authority said on Monday it may announce its decision on the proposed merger between Westpac Banking Corp and the Bank of Melbourne Ltd later this week.
"It will be discussed at the commission this week and there may be a decision this week and there may not," an Australian Competition and Consumer Commission spokeswoman told Reuters.
But she stressed that it was only a possibility.
In April, Westpac offered A$9.75 a share for the Bank of Melbourne, valuing the regional bank at about A$1.4 billion.

ACCC chairman Alan Fels has said recently that the delay in the decision was a result of ongoing inquiries into the merger's effect on competition for transaction accounts, like cheque and savings accounts, and credit cards.
At 0045 GMT (10.45 a.m.), Westpac shares were down seven cents at A$7.98, while Bank of Melbourne stock was steady at A$9.38.
